# ISSUE-36 · Bring FORGE into the BBS

Add an optional contribution desk at DEEP FIELD → DIRECTORY → FORGE. Both routes show the same seven proposal forms and real contributor credits. The service-panel discovery keeps its own gate, story text and ECHO reaction. Generate the credits from validated, shipped attribution during the Vite build and load them on FORGE activation.

## Dimensions

The approved WorkUnit is `multi_area` with the `detailed` profile. Advisory uncertainty is `known` and risk is `standard`. The changes span the content compiler, an optional UI route, issue forms and tests. Budget about 6–10 hours across review, implementation and validation, including a bundle-size iteration, within the approved 32-hour claim budget. The existing agent plan gate applies.

## What we know

- The hub calls `buildTools`, which evaluates each artifact's `requires`, prints its description, opens its links, and grants its `grantsOnOpen`. FORGE requires `flag:service-panel-open`. The code puzzle grants that fact, and `flag:forge-opened` selects ECHO's reaction. Episode 000 completion uses exactly its three declared puzzles, and DEEP FIELD is available after completion. [`src/app/tools.ts:188`](../../src/app/tools.ts#L188) · `content/artifacts/forge.json:4` · `content/puzzles/service-panel.json:5–9` · `content/characters/echo.json:305–312` · `src/puzzle/game.ts:52–64` · `content/episodes/episode-000.json:4` · `content/bbs/deep-field.json:5`
- The signed-in BBS already has Directory, Back and contextual Help. `OPEN <id>` selects a door only on the Doors screen. The door session forwards dispatch results to the view, and the terminal already provides a tool panel. [`src/bbs/bbs.ts:255`](../../src/bbs/bbs.ts#L255) · `src/bbs/bbs.ts:313–332,489–530,600–614` · `src/bbs/door-session.ts:47–55` · `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:29–73` · `src/terminal/terminal.ts:141–155`
- FORGE currently has two issue-form links and a bare repository link. The existing test ignores URLs with no `template` query, so it would accept that repository link despite the new every-link criterion. Plain anchors already use `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. [`content/artifacts/forge.json:17`](../../content/artifacts/forge.json#L17) · `tests/unit/contribution.test.ts:26–58` · `src/world/artifact-view.ts:4–16`
- The reviewed First Light package credits `SIGNAL//LOST maintainers` with handle `supernovae`. Its two entries inherit the entire attribution through `loadContent`. An authored entry attribution takes precedence. The two declarative doors have the collective byline `SIGNAL//LOST contributors` with no named identity, handle or PR. The shared attribution schema currently has author, handle and source PR fields. The separately registered TypeScript door metadata lives in `src/`, and the three `content/code-doors/*.jsonc` gameplay assets have no attribution. The approved design distinguishes real credits from fictional handles, signatures and dates. [`content/community/first-light.json:4`](../../content/community/first-light.json#L4) · `src/content/schema.ts:25–35,437–446` · `src/content/validate.ts:157–181` · `content/doors/relay-trivia.json:6` · `content/doors/forgotten-archive.json:6–8` · `src/doors/code-doors.ts:5–38` · `docs/game-design.md:200–204`
- The merged authoring kit includes the checked starter, local checker, dev-only preview and documented code-door registration path. Its existing tests exercise a copied door in a temporary content tree and assert that preview code stays out of the production build. [`docs/door-authoring.md:5`](../../docs/door-authoring.md#L5) · `tests/unit/contribution.test.ts:125–270` · `tests/unit/content.test.ts:1502–1567`
- The planner ran `npm run build` offline on an unchanged scratch copy of the provided base with Node 24.22.3. Measuring the emitted files with the `Browser tests` method (`gzipSync(readFileSync(file)).length / 1024`) gave `index-LWnyy-94.js` at **60,789 bytes (59.364 KiB)** and `environment-esavcwi0.js` at **132,330 bytes (129.229 KiB)**. The entry has 651 gzip bytes of headroom. The scratch snapshot has no Git metadata. Its scoped build-input fingerprint and measurement command are in TEST_PLAN.md. [`tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts:6`](../../tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts#L6) · `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3–5`

## What we're assuming

- The BBS visit is a read-only contribution route. Treat `forge-opened` as the existing physical terminal discovery, because it drives ECHO's service-panel reaction. Test that a BBS visit leaves the flag and hub tool gate untouched and that a subsequent panel visit still produces the reaction.
- The two existing collective door bylines are placeholders for FORGE credits. Apply that editorial classification in the two authored attribution objects and keep their door bylines visible. Compare the emitted record with authored data, and vary the byline text in a fixture to verify that exclusion follows the declaration.

## Open questions

- The candidate's production gzip sizes are open until the developer builds the actual emitted site in step 4. Browser execution and visual verification belong to the existing `Browser tests` workflow, since the planner's Chromium capability is disabled. CI checks the real production entry, startup, keyboard navigation and the visual distinction.
- Execution paths in scope are Codex on the native isolated Linux backend for source, Node, Vitest and gzip checks, and GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` with Playwright Chromium for browser checks. The repository selects the native backend and Codex developer/tester roles in `.swarm/config.yaml:4–8,16–18,59–67`. Playwright builds and serves `dist/` by interception under `/signal-lost/` (`playwright.config.ts:5–16`, `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3–5`, `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:18–38`, `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11–25`). Other harnesses, operating systems and the live site have no task-specific verification requirement.

## Implementation

### Response to plan review

- **F1.** Step 3 declares maintainer and placeholder classifications in the shipped attribution data. It defines a pure `selectContributorStatus` using exact author/handle identities and makes its result drive the copy in both routes. The A3 Vitest checks in TEST_PLAN.md assert `maintainers-only` for the shipped record, `contributors` for the same tree with one reviewed non-maintainer added, and `empty` for the empty record. They also vary the declared bylines to prove both classifications come from content.

### 1. Add the second route and share the panel

1. Extend `artifactSchema` in `src/content/schema.ts:563` with optional `bbsBoard`, a reference to a BBS endpoint of kind `board`. Validate the reference in `checkReferences` at `src/content/validate.ts:816`, alongside artifact validation, producing a file and field error for a missing endpoint or a reference to another BBS record kind. Existing artifact JSON remains valid without the field.
2. Set `bbsBoard: "deep-field"` in `content/artifacts/forge.json` and add a short Directory/FORGE hint to the completed-episode status in `content/bbs/deep-field.json:21`. Retain the existing hub `requires`, description and `grantsOnOpen`. Keep `buildTools`, service code and story conditions intact.
3. Extend `BbsOffer` and `getBbsOffer` (`src/bbs/offer.ts:16–35,70–83`) to select artifacts for the offered endpoint. In `src/bbs/bbs.ts`, add an `artifact` phase and an `opensArtifact` dispatch result. Add an `OPEN <id>` action to the signed-in Directory using the artifact's name. Dispatch only from Directory and resolve the same offered records used to draw the actions. Back returns to Directory, Menu returns to the signed-in menu, and Disconnect uses the existing route. A visit needs no artifact save effect, progress flag, history entry or schema migration.
4. In `createBbsScene` (`src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:9,29–73`), use the shared `openArtifact` for an `opensArtifact` result and close that panel on leaving the artifact phase. Keep login and settings panel ownership, terminal focus and help behavior. The same seven plain anchors are available in both routes. BBS uses its own directory context, while the hub still prints the physical terminal description and reacts to its grant.

### 2. Add the five no-code proposals

1. Add these issue forms in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, using the existing transmission and archive forms as the YAML and intake model.

   | Form | Ask for |
   | --- | --- |
   | `propose-character.yml` | Fictional name, role, relationship to the network and a sample voice or encounter |
   | `propose-branching-adventure.yml` | Starting situation, player choices and the consequences or endings |
   | `propose-door-game.yml` | Player goal, actions, feedback and completion or replay loop |
   | `propose-network-location.yml` | Site, reason to visit, how it is reached and what a player finds |
   | `propose-mechanic-improvement.yml` | Current interaction, problem, proposed change and an observable improvement |

   Each form says “No code needed,” labels the issue `swarm:community`, and explains review before inclusion. Follow the current model for optional real credit and permission to contribute. Keep fictional details in dedicated fields.
2. Add one anchor for each new form to FORGE's `links` in `content/artifacts/forge.json`. Keep both existing issue-form targets and the filing-office story references. Drop the bare repository anchor so every FORGE anchor points to a form. Use HTTPS URLs on the existing repo's `issues/new?template=…` path.
3. Add an agent-assisted contribution section to `docs/swarmos.md` before “Complete a WorkUnit.” Describe idea intake, review and attribution, optional SwarmOS for approved work, and the existing content and door authoring guides. Link to the merged starter/checker/preview documentation through those guides and retain the ordinary PR route.

### 3. Generate and render the reviewed credits

1. Extend the shared attribution schema in `src/content/schema.ts:25` with optional `creditKind: "maintainer" | "placeholder"`. Omission is ordinary reviewed credit. A placeholder describes an unqualified byline and cannot carry `handle` or `sourcePr`. Mark the existing reviewed package attribution in `content/community/first-light.json:4` as `maintainer`, and mark the existing author bylines in `content/doors/relay-trivia.json:6` and `content/doors/forgotten-archive.json:6` as `placeholder`. Preserve author strings, handles and door metadata behavior. Document in the new `docs/swarmos.md` section that ordinary submissions use standard attribution and maintainers review these classifications.
2. Add `src/content/contributors.ts` with pure functions `buildContributorRecord(content)` and `selectContributorStatus(entries, declaredMaintainers)`. Collect only schema-validated `attribution` on shipped records in the normalized `Content`, including community packages and their flattened entries. Skip attributions tagged `placeholder`. Derive `declaredMaintainers` from the remaining attributions tagged `maintainer`, using exact `author` plus optional `handle` as the identity for both membership and deduplication. Collapse inherited package credit and other repeats, honor explicit entry overrides, and sort identities and unique authored `sourcePr` values deterministically. The selector returns `empty` for zero entries, `maintainers-only` for a nonempty record whose every identity is declared a maintainer, and `contributors` otherwise. A different handle is a different identity even when the author matches. The builder returns `{ entries, status }` using this selector. Real author and placeholder labels are data. Story fields such as `from`, character names, BBS handles, dates and signatures supply no credit. Test fixtures and TypeScript door registrations are outside the shipped attribution source.
3. Add `src/content/contributors-browser.ts` exporting `loadBundledContributors`, with dev parity through `loadBundledContent` and the same pure builder. In `scripts/content-plugin.ts:7–33`, build the record and status after existing validation passes and replace that module in production with serialized data. Register the same authored-source watch paths for the replacement. Keep the validated browser content payload and manifest exports compatible. The `.jsonc` door assets stay with their existing lazy consumers and build inputs stay local.
4. Add optional `contributorRecord` copy to `artifactSchema` and FORGE JSON, with a heading, review explanation, maintainers-only statement, empty message and load-failure message. In `src/world/artifact-view.ts:4–16`, render the existing anchors synchronously and dynamically import a new `src/world/contributor-view.ts` only for an artifact with this copy. Render the “Real contributor credits” section from `loadBundledContributors`. Use the generated `status` to show the maintainer statement for `maintainers-only`, the empty message for `empty`, and only the review explanation and list for `contributors`. Both nonempty states render names and supplied handles and PR values as text. Keep the links usable if the optional chunk fails. Use a per-open mount node so a stale load cannot overwrite another panel or reopen one after Back or Disconnect.
5. Give the contributor section its own layout and styling in `src/style.css` near `.artifact-links`. Use a framed section with a heading and list, visibly distinct from the fictional log output and its origin badges. Use existing theme variables, keep visible focus and wrapping on form links, and leave credits as text rendered through DOM text nodes. The BBS connection and generated contributor module stay outside the startup request graph.

### 4. Check the acceptance paths and production budget

Extend the tests listed in the handoff and run the developer checks in TEST_PLAN.md. Measure the actual `dist/assets/index-*.js` immediately after the first complete implementation build. Use the same gzip computation and cap as CI, then record both the entry and environment sizes for the final candidate. If the entry exceeds 60 KiB, keep contributor-only imports and presentation logic in the lazy view, tighten the short authored copy and remeasure. Preserve the startup request graph, code-door laziness and the 60/170 KiB caps. Use the existing CI workflow for the complete Playwright run.

## HANDOFF

### Touchpoints and dependencies

| Hub and story | `src/app/tools.ts:145,188` `buildTools`; `content/artifacts/forge.json:4–16`; `content/puzzles/service-panel.json:5–9`; `content/characters/echo.json:305`; `content/episodes/episode-000.json:4` | Keep the physical route, its grant and independent completion. Shared renderer gains optional credits. |
| BBS | `src/bbs/offer.ts:16,31` `BbsOffer`, `getBbsOffer`; `src/bbs/bbs.ts:13,53,150,255,313,489,600` `Route`, `DispatchResult`, `screen`, `back`, `dispatch`; `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:9,29` `createBbsScene`, `run`; `content/bbs/deep-field.json:16` | Directory action and panel lifecycle after sign-in. Keep `src/main.ts:143` and the result passthrough in `src/bbs/door-session.ts:52–54`. |
| Content and production | `src/content/schema.ts:25,563` attribution, `artifactSchema`; `src/content/validate.ts:111,157,816` `loadContent`, `checkReferences`; `content/community/first-light.json:4`; `content/doors/relay-trivia.json:6`; `content/doors/forgotten-archive.json:6`; `scripts/content-plugin.ts:7,15,21` `contentPlugin`; `src/content/browser.ts:7` `loadBundledContent` | Validate the route reference and optional copy. Classify the existing attributions in content, then build the record and status with the pure generator and serve them through the lazy module. |
| Renderer | `src/world/artifact-view.ts:4` `openArtifact`; `src/style.css:323,366,592` BBS output, origin badges and artifact links | Share anchors and contributor panel. Keep contributor styling and output separate from the fictional log. |
| Intake | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/propose-transmission.yml:1`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/propose-archive-entry.yml:1`, `docs/swarmos.md:3–7` | Add five forms and extend the guide through existing authoring-kit paths. |

The approved base snapshot has no files at `src/content/contributors.ts`, `src/content/contributors-browser.ts`, `src/world/contributor-view.ts`, or the five form paths named in step 2. Each was checked individually. All other listed implementation files already exist. There are no file removals or renames.

### Tests, fixtures and focused commands

- Extend `tests/unit/contribution.test.ts:24–83` for the seven-link assertion and keep the existing client check and authoring-kit suites. Extend `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:67–106,112–151,468–506` for the signed-in Directory cases. Extend `tests/unit/episode.test.ts:178–189` to assert completion with both optional flags absent. Keep `tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json` for existing compatibility cases. A fresh episode playthrough supplies the independent, no-panel browser state.

Use in-test temporary fixtures, keeping them outside shipped `content/`.

The existing `tests/e2e/budget.spec.ts:6–16` stays authoritative for the CI gzip measurement.

Run the exact **Production gzip check** in TEST_PLAN.md, which includes `npm run build`, and the **Changed-file diagnostics** on that candidate. CI runs `npm run test:e2e` via `Browser tests`. TEST_PLAN.md specifies evidence ownership and reuse.

### Checked assumptions and reopening conditions

- Source searches confirmed the registration, fixtures and authoring kit exist at the approved base. First Light's child entries inherit the whole package attribution. Code-door metadata is validated separately and excluded from the normalized content collection used by the generator. The raw door bylines are retained as display metadata and their new tags determine inclusion in FORGE.
